newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Mine kills five in northern Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Mine kills five in northern Sri Lanka.

text.p: A Tamil Tiger landmine killed at least three Sri Lankan soldiers and two civilians in the northern Jaffna peninsula, a military spokesman said on Monday.

"Terrorists set off a claymore mine in the Valikamam South division of Jaffna around 6.30 p.m. (on Sunday) when one of our patrols was returning to base," he said. "Three soldiers and two civilians, a father and his child, were killed."
Three soldiers and four civilians were wounded, he added.
The army captured the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of Colombo, in April after a series of offensives against Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels.

But the rebels, fighting for a homeland for minority Tamils in the mainly Sinhalese island's north and east, have managed to infiltrate the area in small groups and carry out hit-and-run attacks, military officials said.
A Sri Lankan human rights group said on Saturday the Tigers were trying to attack the army in the presence of civilians in an effort to provoke reprisals by soldiers.
"Despite LTTE provocation and indiscriminate attacks in public places, there have been no reprisals by the army," the University Teachers for Human Rights, Jaffna (UTHR) said in a report.
